Status is awaited because no reported result was verified, not because the source document states a trial state. The axes are taken from the source document's design line, a randomised phase 2 comparison, and its story line; the document gives no primary endpoint, so endpoint is omitted, and it gives no number of previous lines, so the 1L tag is read from the induction-versus-immediate framing of the design. trials.result: Relative change from baseline in Ki67 was a geometric least-squares mean of -75.9% (95% CI -81.9 to -67.9) for amcenestrant 400 mg, -68.2% (-75.7 to -58.4) for amcenestrant 200 mg and -77.7% (-83.4 to -70.0) for letrozole. trials.note: The publication does not state a trial phase. This is a 14-day preoperative window study with a pharmacodynamic endpoint, so it measures proliferation suppression and not disease outcome, and it cannot stand in for an adjuvant efficacy trial. n is the safety population of 104 who received at least one dose; the Ki67 comparison rests on the modified intent-to-treat population of 95 with paired values. Enrollment was stopped early for slow recruitment during the COVID-19 pandemic, so the arms are smaller than planned.

trials.topic: a brain-penetrating peptide-drug conjugate for recurrent brain metastases and leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, reaching-the-compartment
trials.population: Adults with measurable recurrent brain metastases from breast cancer, with or without leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, most of them heavily pretreated.
trials.arms: Single arm of ANG1005 600 mg/m2 intravenously every 3 weeks, with no control arm.
trials.endpoint: Intracranial objective response rate, assessed by CNS RECIST 1.1.
trials.result: The intracranial objective response rate was 15 percent by investigator assessment and 8 percent by independent radiology facility review. The study preset rule for intracranial objective response rate by independent review was not met, and there was no comparator arm.
trials.os: In the leptomeningeal carcinomatosis subset the estimated median overall survival was 8.0 months (95% CI 5.4 to 9.4). No overall survival figure is reported for the whole cohort, and the comparison the authors draw is with historical control rather than a randomised arm.
trials.note: Single-arm study with no randomised comparator for either the parenchymal or the leptomeningeal population. The primary endpoint was formally negative, in that the preset rule for intracranial objective response rate by independent radiology facility review was not met, and the investigator-assessed rate of 15% and the independent rate of 8% should be read separately rather than merged. The 28-patient leptomeningeal carcinomatosis group is a subset of the 72 enrolled patients, so its disease control and survival figures are subgroup results, and the authors' claim of prolonged survival there rests on a comparison with historical control. The abstract gives no NCT identifier and states no hormone receptor or HER2 restriction, so the subtype axis is all comers. The treatment line axis rests on recurrent brain metastases having required prior therapy, with a mean of 2.8 prior CNS-directed therapies, rather than on a stated count of prior systemic lines.

trials.result: Immune activation occurred in 53%, 8 of 15, of cohort A and 60%, 9 of 15, of cohort B, and all cohorts met the Simon two-stage threshold for expansion to stage II. In the TIL-high cohort C, 53%, 8 of 15, had a major pathological response with under 10% viable tumour and 33%, 5 of 15, a pathological complete response.

trials.note: The abstract gives a denominator of 15 for each cohort but no total enrolment, so no participant count is recorded. The cohorts answer different questions. A and B are window-of-opportunity cohorts whose endpoint is immune activation, a laboratory readout rather than a clinical outcome, and only cohort C, restricted to tumours with tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes of 50% or more, took patients to surgery with pathological complete response as its endpoint. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 17% of patients and immune-mediated endocrinopathies in 57%, a high price in early disease. Small selected cohorts and that toxicity mean the trial does not establish that chemotherapy can be omitted.

trials.population: Postmenopausal women aged 18 years or older with untreated clinical T1c to T4a-c oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, an ECOG performance status of 0 to 1 and a baseline Ki67 score of at least 5%.
trials.arms: Giredestrant 30 mg orally daily vs anastrozole 1 mg orally daily on days 1 to 14 as a window-of-opportunity phase, after which both groups continued the same regimen plus palbociclib for four 28-day cycles over a 16-week neoadjuvant phase.

trials.note: The primary endpoint is pharmacodynamic and belongs to the two-week endocrine-only window, before either group received palbociclib, so it compares giredestrant with anastrozole and nothing else. The 16-week neoadjuvant combination phase that follows gave palbociclib to both groups and answers a different question; neither phase establishes survival superiority. The n of 221 is the number enrolled and randomised, while the primary endpoint was assessed only in the subset with complete central Ki67 scores at baseline and week 2, a number the abstract does not give. trials.topic: dual checkpoint blockade in a rare histology, metaplastic breast carcinoma
trials.population: Patients with unresectable or metastatic metaplastic breast cancer, median age 60 years and a median of 2 prior lines of therapy, range none to five.
trials.arms: Single arm of ipilimumab 1 mg/kg intravenously every 6 weeks plus nivolumab 240 mg intravenously every 2 weeks.
trials.endpoint: Objective response rate.
trials.result: The objective response rate was 18%, 3 of 17 patients, with 1 complete and 2 partial responses, which met the primary endpoint; the three responses were ongoing at 28+, 33+ and 34+ months. Median progression-free survival was 2 months.
trials.os: Median overall survival was 12 months.
trials.note: This is one cohort of a rare-tumour basket study rather than a stand-alone trial, and the key is suffixed with the population so that other DART cohorts can be registered separately. Eligibility turned on metaplastic histology and the publication does not report hormone receptor or HER2 status, so the subtype axis is all rather than TNBC even though the record is cross-referenced from metastatic triple-negative disease. Prior therapy ranged from none to five lines, so no single treatment line is assigned. The result is carried by a subset, three exceptional and still ongoing responses against no activity in the rest, in 17 patients, and all three responders developed adrenal insufficiency. A single-arm cohort of this size is a signal in a rare histology and should not be read across to unselected triple-negative disease.

trials.topic: chemotherapy-free maintenance after platinum-sensitive disease, with or without PD-L1 blockade
trials.population: Patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer, defined as estrogen and progesterone receptor expression of 10% or less, with ongoing stable disease or a complete or partial response to first- or second-line platinum-based chemotherapy.
trials.arms: Olaparib 300 mg twice daily alone versus olaparib plus durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1 every 4 weeks, randomized 1:1, each arm judged against a historical control rather than against the other.
trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival compared with a historical control of continued platinum-based therapy.
trials.result: Median progression-free survival from randomization was 4.0 months (95% CI 2.6 to 6.1) with olaparib and 6.1 months (95% CI 3.7 to 10.1) with olaparib plus durvalumab, both significantly longer than the historical control (P = 0.0023 and P < 0.0001 respectively). Clinical benefit rates were 44% (95% CI 23% to 66%) with olaparib alone and 36% (95% CI 17% to 59%) with the combination.
trials.os: Not reported. Overall survival was not an endpoint, and each arm was judged against a historical control rather than against the other.
trials.note: Randomized but non-comparative. Each arm was tested against a historical control of continued platinum-based chemotherapy and the trial was not powered for a head-to-head comparison, so the longer median in the combination arm is not evidence that durvalumab adds benefit. Triple-negative disease was defined at estrogen and progesterone receptor expression of 10% or less and 3 of the 45 patients had expression of 1% to 10%, so the subtype tag is broader than a strict zero-expression definition. Maintenance began after one or two prior lines of platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease, so the line tag is 2L in the sense of prior therapy required rather than a single fixed line. Germline BRCA mutation was not required and the authors single out a BRCA wild-type subset with durable disease control. No overall survival figure is reported, and median follow-up was 9.8 months.

Entry required oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease; central confirmation of androgen receptor positivity was not an entry requirement but defined the evaluable population, which was 102 of the 136 randomly assigned patients, so a quarter of those randomised fall outside the population the primary endpoint describes and the subtype tag carries neither the androgen receptor selection nor that distinction. n is the 136 patients randomly assigned; the primary endpoint was assessed in the 102 with centrally confirmed androgen receptor-positive disease, and the safety denominators of 75 and 61 are all patients who received each dose. Entry required previous treatment but the abstract states no number of previous lines, so the line tag is 3L+ by the registry rule for trials that require prior therapy. trials.population: Patients with progressive HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases.
trials.arms: Single arm of everolimus with trastuzumab and vinorelbine, with no control arm.
trials.endpoint: Intracranial response rate, with a two-stage design built to distinguish an intracranial response rate of 5% from one of 20%.
trials.result: The intracranial response rate was 4 percent, a single partial response. CNS clinical benefit rate was 27 percent at 6 months and 65 percent at 3 months, and there was no comparator arm.
trials.os: Overall survival was 12.2 months (95% CI 0.6 to 20.2), which the authors describe as similar to historical control.
trials.note: The primary endpoint was negative. The single-arm design has no comparator, and the authors read the time to progression and overall survival as similar to historical control. The enrolled count of 32 is the number evaluable for toxicity; only 26 were evaluable for efficacy, so the response figures rest on the smaller group. The correlative finding that PI3K/mTOR pathway mutations were not associated with response is the point of the record, in that a pathway and brain-penetration rationale did not deliver intracranial activity. The published confidence interval for overall survival, 0.6 to 20.2 months, is reproduced as printed. The abstract does not separate hormone receptor positive from hormone receptor negative HER2-positive disease, so the subtype axis stays HER2+, and the treatment line axis rests on entry requiring progressive brain metastases rather than on a stated count of prior lines.

trials.arms: Single arm of enzalutamide 160 mg once daily until disease progression, with no control arm.
trials.endpoint: Clinical benefit rate at 16 weeks, in all enrolled patients and in the evaluable subgroup whose tumours expressed androgen receptor in at least 10% of nuclei.
trials.result: Of 118 patients enrolled, 78 were evaluable. Clinical benefit rate at 16 weeks was 25% (95% CI 17% to 33%) in the intention-to-treat population and 33% (95% CI 23% to 45%) in the evaluable subgroup. Median progression-free survival was 2.9 months (95% CI 1.9 to 3.7) and 3.3 months (95% CI 1.9 to 4.1) respectively.
trials.os: Median overall survival was 12.7 months (95% CI 8.5 to not yet reached) in the intention-to-treat population and 17.6 months (95% CI 11.6 to not yet reached) in the evaluable subgroup.
trials.note: Single arm, so the figures establish that activity exists and not how often it will be seen. Two androgen receptor thresholds are in play and they are not the same thing. Entry required staining above 0%, while the evaluable subgroup required at least 10% of nuclei, which is the threshold TBCRC 011 and TBCRC 032 used for entry. The gap between the two clinical benefit rates is therefore a statement about the assay cut-point rather than about the drug. No androgen receptor directed agent is approved in this setting.

trials.arms: Sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab versus sacituzumab govitecan alone, randomised 1 to 1.
trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival.
trials.result: At 15.5 months median follow-up, sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab did not significantly improve progression-free survival compared with sacituzumab govitecan alone, median 8.4 versus 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.76 (95% CI 0.48 to 1.19), P = 0.12.
trials.os: Median overall survival was 20.0 versus 18.0 months (P = 0.18).
trials.note: The primary endpoint was negative in the population unselected by PD-L1. The PD-L1-positive result is a key secondary analysis in 39 of the 88 patients with evaluable tissue, is not statistically significant, and is described by the authors as a trend warranting investigation in larger randomised trials, so it should be read as hypothesis-generating. Eligibility allowed zero or one prior chemotherapy regimen for metastatic disease on top of prior endocrine therapy and 47% had received no chemotherapy for metastatic disease, so the line tag is a single label for a mixed population and the trial sits earlier than the third-line setting in which sacituzumab govitecan is registered for this subtype. The abstract gives no ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, so no NCT number is recorded.

trials.topic: single-fraction against five-fraction radiotherapy for malignant spinal canal compression, cord-compression
trials.population: Patients with spinal cord or cauda equina compression from metastatic cancer at 42 UK and 5 Australian centres, with life expectancy over 8 weeks and no previous radiotherapy to the same area. 44% had prostate cancer, 19% lung cancer and 12% breast cancer.

trials.note: Breast cancer was 12% of the enrolled population. The primary endpoint was assessed in 342 of 686 patients because the rest had died by week 8, which is the main limit on reading the non-inferiority result. The publication states no phase.

trials.topic: tucatinib with trastuzumab for activating HER2 mutations in HER2-negative disease, HER2-mutant
trials.population: Heavily pretreated women with HER2-mutated metastatic breast cancer that was HER2-negative on local testing, enrolled as one cohort of an open-label basket study of HER2-altered solid tumours; those with hormone receptor-positive disease also received fulvestrant.
trials.arms: Single arm of tucatinib plus trastuzumab, with fulvestrant added for hormone receptor-positive disease.
trials.endpoint: Overall response rate.
trials.result: Overall response rate was 41.9% (90% CI 26.9 to 58.2) in the 31 patients. The secondary endpoints of duration of response and progression-free survival were 12.6 months (90% CI 4.7 to not estimable) and 9.5 months (90% CI 5.4 to 13.8) respectively.
trials.os: Not reported. Overall survival was not an endpoint of this single-arm basket cohort.
trials.note: This is the HER2-mutated breast cohort of a solid-tumour basket study rather than a stand-alone breast trial, and it is single-arm. Entry required an activating HER2 mutation in disease that was HER2-negative by conventional local testing, so it is not a HER2-amplified or first-line HER2-positive trial and belongs with molecular-target evidence. The subtype tag is all because the cohort took both hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative patients within HER2-negative disease; only the hormone receptor-positive patients received fulvestrant, and the abstract gives no split between the two groups. The abstract reports the duration of response and progression-free survival figures without naming a statistic, so the record does not call them medians. Confidence intervals are 90%, not the registry's usual 95%, and the cohort of 31 is small. Patients were heavily pretreated and the abstract states no number of previous lines, so the line tag is 3L+ by the registry rule for trials that require prior therapy.

trials.topic: whether adding PD-L1 blockade to platinum chemotherapy helps in metastatic TNBC
trials.population: Patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer treated at six centres between August 2017 and June 2021; all were female, with a mean age of 55 years (range 27 to 79).
trials.arms: Carboplatin AUC 6 every three weeks alone versus carboplatin AUC 6 with atezolizumab 1200 mg every three weeks, continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
trials.result: Adding atezolizumab improved progression-free survival, hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.44 to 1.01; P = .05), from a median of 2.2 months with carboplatin alone to 4.1 months with the combination. The overall response rate rose from 8.0% (95% CI 3.2% to 18.8%) to 30.4% (95% CI 19.9% to 43.3%).
trials.os: Overall survival improved, hazard ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.96; P = .03), from a median of 8.6 months with carboplatin alone to 12.6 months with carboplatin and atezolizumab.
trials.note: Exploratory randomised phase 2 trial. Its result should not be equated with the confirmatory registration evidence for the approved chemotherapy-immunotherapy regimens in metastatic TNBC. Benefit was seen regardless of PD-L1 status, and the PD-L1-positive subgroup did not benefit more, which runs against the selection strategy used by the phase 3 trials. The abstract sets no prior-therapy requirement and reports prior chemotherapy as a subgroup, so the trial spanned treated and untreated patients and line is recorded as any. All subgroup hazard ratios are exploratory, and each named subgroup carries its own hazard ratio rather than the single one quoted for prior chemotherapy.

trials.topic: BCL2 inhibition added to fulvestrant after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor
trials.population: Pre- and postmenopausal females aged 18 years or older with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer that had progressed after a CDK4/6 inhibitor.
trials.arms: Venetoclax 800 mg orally daily plus fulvestrant versus fulvestrant alone, randomised 1:1.
trials.endpoint: Clinical benefit rate.
trials.result: Venetoclax did not significantly improve clinical benefit rate, which was 11.8% (6 of 51; 95% CI 4.44 to 23.87) with venetoclax plus fulvestrant and 13.7% (7 of 51; 95% CI 5.70 to 26.26) with fulvestrant, a risk difference of -1.96% (95% CI -16.86 to 12.94). Median progression-free survival was 2.69 months (95% CI 1.94 to 3.71) versus 1.94 months (95% CI 1.84 to 3.55), stratified HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.45; P = 0.7853).
trials.os: Overall survival was a secondary endpoint and the data were not mature at the primary analysis.
trials.note: The primary endpoint was negative and that is the substance of the record. The biomarker-defined subgroups with strong BCL2 expression, a BCL2 to BCLXL Histoscore ratio of 1 or more, or PIK3CA wild-type status showed only nonsignificant improvements in exploratory analyses and should not be read as a positive signal. n is the 103 patients at the primary analysis cutoff of August 5, 2020. Venetoclax is tagged as other, since a BCL2 inhibitor has no dedicated modality; no CDK4/6 inhibitor was given on trial, and prior CDK4/6 inhibition is an entry criterion rather than a treatment arm. The abstract states only that disease had progressed after a CDK4/6 inhibitor and was endocrine-therapy resistant, setting no limit on prior lines, so the line axis is 3L+. The abstract gives no NCT number, so that field is omitted.

trials.topic: twelve weeks of anthracycline-free nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy, carboplatin versus gemcitabine, with response used to guide further treatment
trials.population: Patients with triple-negative breast cancer, oestrogen and progesterone receptor under 1% and HER2-negative, cT1c to cT4c, cN0 or node-positive.
trials.arms: Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 with gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks versus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 with carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks, each for 12 weeks.
trials.endpoint: Pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0) by therapy arm; the trial was also powered for early response, defined as a Ki-67 decrease of more than 30% or fewer than 500 invasive tumour cells in the three-week serial biopsy.
trials.result: Pathological complete response was 28.7% (95% CI 0.22 to 0.36) with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine and 45.9% (95% CI 0.38 to 0.54) with nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin, 95% CI for the difference 6.2% to 27.9%, P = .002. Pathological complete response was lower in early non-responders than in early responders, 19.5% versus 44.4%, P < .001, and was 50.0% in patients whose early response was unclassifiable.
trials.os: no survival advantage from carboplatin at a median follow-up of 60 months despite the higher pathological complete response rate, HR 1.04 (0.68-1.59); the final analysis does not report overall survival separately from invasive disease-free survival
trials.note: The tabulated result is the primary pathological complete response comparison from gluz2018. The final analysis, gluz2022, reports no survival advantage for carboplatin despite its higher pathological complete response rate, hazard ratio 1.04 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.59), so the pathological complete response gain here did not become a survival gain. Treatment after the 12 weeks was response-adapted, with omission of further chemotherapy allowed only after pathological complete response, so between-arm survival comparisons are confounded by what patients received next. gluz2022 is indexed in PubMed as an editorial but is the trial's final survival and translational report, and no overall survival figures are given in either abstract. No NCT identifier appears in the abstracts, so none is recorded.

trials.topic: HER2-PET to predict T-DM1 benefit
trials.population: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, immunohistochemistry 3+ or fluorescence in situ hybridisation ratio at least 2.2, scheduled to start trastuzumab emtansine.
trials.arms: Single arm. Pretreatment HER2 positron emission tomography with zirconium-89 labelled trastuzumab, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography at baseline and before cycle 2, in patients all receiving trastuzumab emtansine.
trials.endpoint: Negative and positive predictive values of HER2 positron emission tomography, of early metabolic response, and of the two combined, against morphological response by RECIST 1.1 after three cycles and against time to treatment failure.
trials.result: HER2 imaging was negative in 29% of patients and showed intrapatient heterogeneity in 46%. Negative and positive predictive values against RECIST were 88% and 72% for HER2 imaging and 83% and 96% for early metabolic response. Combining the two gave predictive values of 100% in both directions and separated a group with median time to treatment failure of 2.8 months from one with 15 months. There was no control arm and no randomised allocation by imaging.
trials.os: Not reported. The primary publication reports predictive values and time to treatment failure only.
